stage1.impression: A moody, almost monochrome red frame: a glowing box on a dark plinth before a board-formed wall, with a mirror reflection below. The idea of colour spilling onto concrete reads, but the whole wall is soaked in the same murky red to the corners, so the pool has no shape. The hard lit ledge line, the over-crisp reflection cut off by the frame edge, the near-white ports and the flat, unlit card of a horn all say render more than night photograph.

blocking_9: The colour on the wall must read as a shaped pool that falls off to near black at the frame corners (corner luminance median under 12; it is 23 now, brighter than the wall just above the horn at 20)
No hard, lit horizontal line behind the speaker: the ledge top at y 482-498 is a 2x step over the wall just above it
The floor reflection must be subordinate to the speaker: softer, darker, and not cut off by the bottom edge of the frame
The speaker must sit nearer the optical centre, with the whole object and its pool composed and the ground a quiet base rather than a second subject
Concrete outside the pool must still read as concrete under the moon, not as a flat red veil
The port highlights must hold the Ember hue rather than going pink-white

defects.what: Whole upper wall and both corners washed in the same red (lum ~23, r ~55) as the area above the speaker: the pool has no edge, reads as a red veil or tinted haze, not as light from one lamp
Hard horizontal lit band (the low ledge's top edge) slicing behind the woofer, lum 33 vs 22 just above; reads as a CG shelf line
Hard-edged black wings either side of the pool (left wall lum 7, crush ~1%) with a geometric V outline; the shadow shape draws the eye away from the speaker
Mirror-crisp, bright reflection of the speaker (lum mean 70, as bright as the speaker face) competing with the hero and cut off by the bottom edge
Puddle boundary strip with a diagonal crack crossing the reflection; reads as a texture seam
Port openings near white-pink (r 246, g 202, b 197): the lamp is seen directly and the Ember hue bleaches
Horn reads as a flat dark-red rounded card with a dark blob, unlit (lum 21), floating above the box
Panel joint lines at x~95 and x~718 are razor-hard (16-level step in 0 px) and stop abruptly at the ledge height
Ground outside the reflection crushed to near black with a blue tint (14% crushed), no paving texture legible

changes.problem: The wall glows the same red to every corner, so the colour pool has no shape and the frame reads as a red veil.

evidence.measured: top-left lum_median 23.6 (r 56), top-right 22.7, vs wall directly above the horn [250,150,550,300] 20.3; the corners are as bright as the pool's upper edge

changes.expected: The red scatter veil drops; the pool on the wall near the speaker keeps its brightness (lum ~45-50 at [470,330,600,450]) while the corners fall toward black with a soft, visible gradient between.

changes.problem: The low ledge behind the speaker catches the light as a hard horizontal line across the frame and casts the geometric V-wing shadows.

evidence.measured: lum_median 33.4, p95 75 vs 22.3 in the wall band just above it [240,460,330,476]; profile at x 600-640 steps 41.6 -> 26.7 -> 16.4 across y 425-490

change.setting: set.props.1 (the 0.6 m concrete ledge at y 0.65)
change.to: removed, so the speaker stands 0.75 m clear of an uninterrupted board-formed wall

changes.expected: One continuous wall plane behind the speaker; the light pool rises from the floor line with no shelf edge and no hard wing shadows.

changes.problem: The wet paving acts as a mirror: the reflection is as bright and crisp as the speaker and competes with it.

evidence.measured: reflection lum_mean 69.6, p95 179, about equal to the speaker face [355,435,440,545] lum_mean 71.3

changes.expected: A soft, broken, dimmer reflection under the plinth (roughly half the speaker's brightness) that grounds the speaker without doubling it; the paving texture shows around it.

changes.problem: The speaker sits low, the horn at only 40% of the frame height, and the reflection is cut off by the bottom edge, so the frame is split into a big empty wall and a cropped floor.

evidence.measured: product spans y 322-605 of 800; reflection runs to y 800 and is cropped; upper 320 px is wall only

changes.expected: Speaker centred slightly below the middle and a little larger; the floor occupies the lower fifth with the reflection ending inside the frame; the pool on the wall fills the upper half with room for type.

changes.problem: Outside the pool the concrete is an illegible murk; the moon is too weak to model the board-form texture, so the night has no cool counterpoint to the red.

evidence.measured: lum_median 7.1, lum_range 7 (no texture); upper wall lum_range 12-19

change.to: 0.2 at [7, -3, 6] (lower, more raking across the wall face)

changes.expected: A faint blue-grey raking light picks out the board lines and tie holes at the frame edges, giving a cool field against which the red pool reads as colour, not as a tint.

changes.problem: The port openings bleach to pink-white, losing the speaker's colour at its brightest points.

change.to: local burn on the two port discs of about -0.7 stop (or lights.up0.power_w 225 -> 190 with exposure 1.0 -> 1.1 so the wall holds)

changes.expected: Ports read as hot Ember red with a small brighter core, not white discs.

changes.problem: The puddle boundary crosses the reflection as a lighter strip with a diagonal crack, reading as a texture seam.

evidence.measured: visible lighter band with a diagonal dark line at 3x crop, right under the plinth

change.from: puddle edge falling 0.3 m in front of the plinth
change.to: puddle centred under the plinth so no edge or tile crack crosses the speaker's reflection

changes.expected: The reflection fades out evenly toward the camera with no strip or crack across it.

out_of_scope.request: Make the horn on top read as a lit, three-dimensional cast-resin form rather than a flat dark card
out_of_scope.why: Its shape and the batts that stop the uplight are fixed, and a second light on the horn breaks the one-uplight rule; only the existing light and the moon may model it.

out_of_scope.request: Let more light through the cabinet's upper face so the wall above the horn gets more colour
out_of_scope.why: The lining is fixed and stops light as real batts do.
